subject: history_civics
label: 2022 Sem 1
instructions: All questions are compulsory. The intended marks for questions or parts of questions are given in brackets [].

questions.question: The Lok Sabha session which is conducted in the month of November and December is the .................
questions.solution: (c) Winter Session. Parliament has three sessions a year: Budget (February-March), Monsoon (July-August) and Winter (November-December).

questions.question: The ............ motion allows the house to take up a definite matter of urgent importance.
questions.solution: (b) Adjournment. An Adjournment Motion is laid to discuss a matter of urgent public importance and interrupts the normal business of the House.

questions.question: Which of these denotes the correct composition of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution: (b) 238 elected + 12 nominated. Of 250 members, 12 are nominated by the President and 238 are elected representatives of the States and Union Territories.

questions.question: What is the quorum of the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution: (c) 1/10. Quorum is fixed at 1/10th of the total membership of each House.

concepts: Speaker election by Lok Sabha members
questions.question: Which of these statements regarding the Speaker is false?

options.a: He/She is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha.
options.b: Elected from among the members of the Lok Sabha.
options.c: Elected when the newly elected house meets for the first time.
options.d: The members of both the houses vote to choose the Speaker.

questions.solution: (d) The members of both the houses vote to choose the Speaker.. The Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha only, when the newly elected House meets for the first time.

concepts: Rajya Sabha permanent house, 1/3 retire every 2 years
questions.question: The Rajya Sabha is called a Permanent house because 1/3 members retire every.............. .
questions.solution: (a) two years. It does not dissolve as a whole; every two years one-third of the members retire and fresh elections take place. Members are elected for 6 years.

concepts: Article 249 exclusive power of Rajya Sabha
questions.question: Which of these is considered to be an exclusive power of the Rajya Sabha?

options.a: It can approve an Ordinary Bill.
options.b: It can make amendments to the Constitution.
options.c: It can empower Parliament to make laws on the State list.
options.d: It can make laws on subjects in the Union List.

questions.solution: (c) It can empower Parliament to make laws on the State list.. Under Article 249 the Rajya Sabha, by a 2/3rd majority resolution, can empower Parliament to make laws on a matter in the State List.

questions.question: In case of a conflict between the Centre and the State with reference to a subject in the Concurrent list ................ .

options.c: The President is empowered to decide.

questions.solution: (d) The Union law will prevail.. In case of conflict the law of the Centre prevails and the state law is considered abolished.

questions.question: The right of the members to ..................... is known as interpellation.
questions.solution: (a) Ask questions. One hour a day is reserved for questions; the right of asking questions is the Right of Interpellation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Ordinances is false?

options.b: Issued when the Parliament is not in session.
options.c: Has to be approved within six months from the re-assembly of the Parliament.
options.d: Has to be approved by both the houses of the Parliament.

questions.solution: (c) Has to be approved within six months from the re-assembly of the Parliament.. An ordinance ceases to exist if Parliament takes no action within six weeks of reassembly (maximum life six months and six weeks), so 'six months from re-assembly' is false.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a qualification required to be a member of the Rajya Sabha?

options.a: Should be a citizen of India.
options.c: Should be at least 30 year of age.
options.d: Should be a graduate from any university in India.

questions.solution: (d) Should be a graduate from any university in India.. A member must be an Indian citizen, at least 30 years old, on the electoral list and hold no office of profit; no graduation is required.

concepts: Indirect election of Rajya Sabha by MLAs
questions.question:
Complete the given analogy.
Election of Lok sabha member: Citizens of India
Election of Rajya Sabha member: ..............................
questions.solution: (a) Members of the Legislative Assembly.. Elected members of the Rajya Sabha are elected indirectly by members of the State Legislative Assemblies by Single Transferable Vote.

questions.question:
Lok Sabha members from States: 530
Lok Sabha members from Union territories: ?
questions.solution: (c) 20. The Constitution (Article 81, as taught in the ICSE text) provides a maximum of 550 members in the Lok Sabha: 530 from the States and 20 from the Union Territories.

concepts: Extension of Lok Sabha term during National Emergency
questions.question: Under what circumstances may the term of the Lok Sabha be extended by one year at a time?
questions.solution: (b) Proclamation of a National Emergency. The term is 5 years but can be extended by one year at a time during a proclamation of emergency.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT refer to the control of the Parliament over the Executive?
questions.solution: (b) Amendment of Constitution. Parliament controls the Executive through interpellation, no-confidence motion, adjournment motion, censure motion and monetary control; amendment of the Constitution is not one.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution: (a) A.O. Hume. The INC was formed by Allan Octavian Hume, a retired civil servant, with national leaders in December 1885.

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
concepts: Dates of Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience movements
questions.question:
Complete the Analogy.
Non-Cooperation Movement: 1920 : : Civil Disobedience Movement : ........................ .
questions.solution: (d) 1930. Non-Cooperation was launched in 1920; Civil Disobedience in April 1930.

questions.question: Which of these statement is NOT associated with Jyotiba Phule?

options.c: He established the Satya Shodak Samaj.
options.d: He was against the caste system.

questions.solution: (b) He established the Brahmo Samaj.. Phule founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj in 1873; the Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828.

questions.chapter: First Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Early Nationalists is false?

options.a: Their leaders were Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
options.b: They believed in constitutional means of protest.
options.c: They wanted self-government under British rule.
options.d: They wanted to launch violent agitations against the British.

questions.solution: (d) They wanted to launch violent agitations against the British.. Early Nationalists used constitutional, peaceful methods.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question: When was Bengal partitioned?
questions.solution: (a) 1905. Announced 20 July 1905 by Lord Curzon, implemented 16 October 1905.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
concepts: Nationalist view of Partition of Bengal: divide and rule
questions.question: Which of the following was a nationalist perspective of the Partition of Bengal?

options.a: There were only Hindus in West Bengal.
options.b: To divide the Hindus and Muslims.
options.c: There were many riots in Bengal.
options.d: It was an administrative necessity as Bengal was a large territory.

questions.solution: (b) To divide the Hindus and Muslims.. Nationalists believed the partition was meant to break Hindu-Muslim unity.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question: From the given list, identify the objective of the Muslim League.

options.a: To train and organise public opinion in the country.
options.b: To promote friendly relations between nationalists political workers.
options.c: To promote among Muslims of India support for the British Government.

questions.solution: (c) To promote among Muslims of India support for the British Government.. Aims of the Muslim League: promote loyalty towards the British among Muslims, protect Muslims' political rights, prevent hostility between Muslims and other communities.

questions.chapter: First Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
Replace the underlined word and correct the statement
Surendranath Banerjee presided over the Second Session of the Indian National Congress.
questions.solution: (a) Dadabhai Naoroji. The Second Congress Session (Calcutta, 1886) was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
concepts: Jallianwala Bagh and its link to movements
questions.question: Which of these statements is NOT associated with the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?

options.b: General Dyer was responsible for the massacre.
options.c: It became a cause for the Non-Cooperation Movement.
options.d: It became a cause for the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.solution: (d) It became a cause for the Civil Disobedience Movement.. The massacre (13 April 1919) was a cause of the Non-Cooperation Movement; Civil Disobedience was launched in 1930.

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
questions.question: The Khilafat Movement was started under the leadership of ......................... .
questions.solution: (a) Ali Brothers. Launched by Shaukat Ali and Mohammad Ali to stop the British abolishing the caliphate.

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
concepts: Chauri Chaura and suspension of Non-Cooperation
questions.question: What was the cause for the sudden suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
questions.solution: (b) The Chauri-Chaura Incident. At Chauri Chaura on 5 February 1922 a mob burnt twenty-two policemen; Gandhiji withdrew the movement on 12 February 1922.

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
questions.question: How did the Lahore session of 1929 lead to the Civil Disobedience Movement?

options.a: The Declaration of Poorna Swaraj was passed
options.b: Subash Chandra Bose was made the President of the Congress
options.d: Congress passed a resolution to begin the Civil Disobedience Movement

questions.solution: (a) The Declaration of Poorna Swaraj was passed. The 1929 Lahore session under Nehru adopted the resolution of complete independence (Poorna Swaraj), declared 26 January 1930 as Independence Day, and the movement began in April 1930.

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
concepts: Causes of Quit India: Cripps failure, Japanese threat
questions.question: What were the causes of the Quit India Movement?

options.a: Failure of Simon Commission and Rowlatt Act.
options.b: Failure of the Cripps Mission and Declaration of Poorna Swaraj.
options.c: Growing Unemployment and Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.
options.d: Failure of Cripps Mission and Japanese threat.

questions.solution: (d) Failure of Cripps Mission and Japanese threat.. Launched August 1942 owing to Japanese invasions in South-East Asia and failure of the Cripps Mission.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a clause of the Indian Independence Act of 1947?

options.a: All treaties made with the British would lapse.
options.b: The army and assets would belong only to India.
options.c: The Constituent Assemblies would serve as Central Legislatures.
options.d: The Princely States were free to associate themselves with either dominion.

questions.solution: (b) The army and assets would belong only to India.. The army, administrative services, assets and liabilities were to be divided between the two new states.

questions.question: Identify the famous slogan of Subhas Chandra Bose.

options.a: Give me blood and I shall give you freedom.
options.b: Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.

questions.solution: (a) Give me blood and I shall give you freedom.. Bose gave the call 'Give me blood and I shall get you freedom' on setting up the Provisional Government of Free India (21 October 1943).

concepts: Reasons for acceptance of Mountbatten Plan
questions.question: Which of the following was a reason for the acceptance of the Mountbatten Plan?

options.a: The British forced the Congress to accept the plan.
options.b: The Muslim League would cooperate in the governance.
options.c: The only alternative to partition was a Federation with a weak Centre.
options.d: The princely States wanted to accept the plan.

questions.solution: (c) The only alternative to partition was a Federation with a weak Centre.. Partition and framing own Constitution would leave India with a strong Centre and remove divisive factors like separate electorates.

questions.question: Which of the following was an objective of the Indian National Army?

options.a: To formulate and present the demands to the government.
options.b: To make the world aware of the true nature of British rule in India.
options.c: Total mobilization of Indian manpower and money for a total war.
options.d: To establish Home Rule in India.

questions.solution: (c) Total mobilization of Indian manpower and money for a total war.. The INA aimed to regain freedom by waging war on the British, mobilising Indian manpower and money.

concepts: Greased cartridges as immediate cause of 1857
questions.question:
India's first war of independence, better known as the Indian Rebellion of 1857, began on, May 10 in the year 1857. The first martyr of the revolt was Mangal Pandey and the war was the result of accumulation of many factors over time. The rebellion of 1857 is considered the first blow that came to shatter the British rule in India. Some epicenters of the revolt were- Kanpur, Lucknow, Aligarh, Agra, Delhi and Jhansi. Due to all the epicenters being far from each other, there was a communication gap between the leadership, it got limited to some parts of India only, Rebels did not have enough weapons and finance whereas British People had advanced weapons and enough finance. (India Today)

Identify the immediate cause of the above revolt.

options.b: The inhuman treatment of indigo cultivators.

questions.solution: (d) The incident of greased cartridges.. The new Enfield rifle used greased paper cartridges that sepoys had to bite; rumours said the grease was animal fat.

Which policy of expansion led to the annexation of Awadh?
questions.solution: (c) Pretext of alleged misrule. Awadh was annexed on grounds of maladministration and misgovernance.

questions.solution: (a) Taxing religious places.. Imposing taxes on temples and religious places was a socio-religious cause.

The British showed total disregard towards the soldiers. In this context, which of the following statement is NOT true?

options.b: They were forced to go overseas on duty.
options.c: They were given the same salaries as that of the British soldiers.
options.d: The chances of promotion were very bleak.

questions.solution: (c) They were given the same salaries as that of the British soldiers.. Indian soldiers were paid less than British soldiers.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
Look at the picture given below and answer the questions that follow: [Picture of three Indian nationalist leaders]
Identify the leaders in the picture.

options.a: Surendranath Banerjee, Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale
options.b: Dadabhai Naoroji, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal
options.c: Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Dadabhai Naoroji
options.d: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal

questions.solution: (d) Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal. The leaders are Lal-Bal-Pal.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
Look at the picture given below and answer the questions that follow: [Picture of three Indian nationalist leaders]
Which group of Congress did they belong to?
questions.solution: (b) Assertive Nationalists. They were Assertive (Radical) Nationalists, who disagreed with the Moderates' methods.
questions.figure_desc: Picture of three Assertive (Radical) Nationalist leaders of the Congress, to be identified from the image.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
Look at the picture given below and answer the questions that follow: [Picture of three Indian nationalist leaders]
What was their main objective?

options.d: Demand for Provincial Government for Indians.

questions.solution: (a) Attainment of Poorna Swaraj. Immediate attainment of Swaraj was the main objective of the Assertive Nationalists.
questions.figure_desc: Picture of three Assertive (Radical) Nationalist leaders of the Congress, to be identified from the image.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
Look at the picture given below and answer the questions that follow: [Picture of three Indian nationalist leaders]
What are the methods associated with them?

options.c: Sending deputation of Indian leaders to Britain
options.d: Sending petitions to the British government

questions.solution: (b) Swadeshi and Boycott. Passive resistance, non-cooperation, boycott of government services/courts/schools and foreign goods, and Swadeshi.
